name: Phone booth

parts.name: kiosk body
parts.massBasis: Kiosk body is a hollow shell (four walls, roof, heavy base, internal phone hardware) of cast-iron/steel and glass, ~1.25×1.25×3.25 m. Classic K6-style booths weigh ~750 kg total; subtracting the door gives ~700 kg. Center of mass is slightly below mid-height because of the heavy base slab. Cross-sectional variance (x,y) ≈0.20 reflects mass concentrated in thin perimeter walls (hollow-box distribution approaching 0.25); vertical variance ≈0.08 because walls, roof, and floor spread mass nearly uniformly along the 3.25 m height.

parts.name: door
parts.massBasis: Phone-booth door is a thin framed panel (glass + metal/wood frame, ~78 mm thick). Mass ~30 kg typical for a glazed kiosk door. Center slightly below mid-height due to heavier lower rail and handle hardware. Variance near 1/12 on all axes: thickness is small but mass fills it fairly uniformly; width and height distributions are roughly uniform across the panel.
